carcacite.name: La Cité de Carcassonne
carcacite.slogan: Two rings of walls, and a skyline drawn for fairy tales.
carcacite.line: Eugène Viollet-le-Duc restored the fortress between 1853 and 1879, and its 1997 UNESCO listing cites that very restoration.

peyrepertuseaude.name: Peyrepertuse
peyrepertuseaude.slogan: A Cathar fortress stretched along a ridge, above the clouds.
peyrepertuseaude.line: Perched at about 800 metres, its upper keep was ordered by King Louis IX in 1242 and reached by a staircase cut into the rock.

carcaloucabaret.name: Canal du Midi
carcaloucabaret.slogan: Plane trees, slow locks and the Cité drifting past the bow.
carcaloucabaret.line: Begun under Pierre-Paul Riquet after Louis XIV's edict of 1666, the canal opened in 1681 and became a UNESCO site in 1996.

lastoursfour.name: Châteaux de Lastours
lastoursfour.slogan: Four castles on one ridge, and one stubborn Cathar stronghold.
lastoursfour.line: Cabaret, the best preserved of the four, held out against Simon de Montfort's crusaders for about two years before surrendering.

fontfroideabbey.name: Fontfroide Abbey
fontfroideabbey.slogan: Pink stone, a quiet cloister and roses in the Corbières hills.
fontfroideabbey.line: Founded in 1093 by Aimery, Viscount of Narbonne, it joined the Cistercian order around 1145.
